matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the Abstract claims T = d^{O(1/ε)} for the simplex case, but the actual theorem gives d^{O(1/ε²)}. Pred_id 3 explicitly states the Abstract's d^{O(1/ε)} contradicts Theorem 1.1 and Corollary C.5's d^{O(1/ε²)} bound.

Both identify that the Abstract overstates the tightness of the lower bound. Pred_id 9 notes the lower bound is exp(Ω(ε^{-1/6})) while the upper bound is exp(O(1/ε²)), showing a polynomial gap in the exponent, not tightness 'up to constant factors'.
Both identify the fabricated citation [ZKL23]. Pred_id 2 explicitly states this citation appears in the Introduction but has no matching bibliography entry, confirming it is fabricated.

Both identify the reversed Bregman divergence definition. Pred_id 1 explicitly notes the definition has the gradient evaluated at y instead of p, contradicting the standard convention used throughout the paper and breaking the theoretical foundation.
Both identify that TreeCal's claim of not requiring knowledge of ρ is false. Pred_id 11 notes the Abstract claims 'no knowledge of ρ' but the proof sets L = 12ρ/ε, requiring ρ to set parameters.

While pred_id 14 discusses TreeSwap attribution confusion, it focuses on whether TreeSwap is novel vs. prior work, not the specific contradiction about the algorithm being 'nearly identical' to [Pen25] while claiming analytical novelty. The issues are related but distinct.

Both address the claim about dimension-independence for the ℓ2 ball. Pred_id 13 notes the claim is misleading because diameter is only dimension-free under specific unit-ball normalization, matching the ground truth's concern about hidden dimension dependence.

Both identify the incorrect strong convexity definition. Pred_id 6 explicitly states the definition uses ≤ instead of ≥, which is a smoothness-type inequality rather than strong convexity, matching the ground truth exactly.

The ground truth concerns the phrase 'completely solves' being an overstatement. While pred_id 13 discusses dimension-independence claims, none of the findings address the specific rhetorical exaggeration about 'completely solving' the problem.
Both identify the incorrect constant in Theorem C.1. Pred_id 7 notes the theorem states b/L but the proof uses 3ρ/L (with b = ρ), meaning the constant 3 is missing from the theorem statement.
The ground truth concerns missing funding disclosure and conflict of interest statements. None of the findings address ethical integrity or funding disclosure issues.

Both identify the BTL implementability contradiction. Pred_id 10 explicitly notes Section 3.3 claims BTL can be implemented with lookahead while Appendix C.2 states it is unimplementable, matching the ground truth's logical inconsistency.

Both address confusion about TreeSwap attribution. Pred_id 14 notes the paper is inconsistent about whether TreeSwap is novel or from prior work [DDFG24, PR24], matching the ground truth's concern about misattribution.

Both identify the inequality direction error in Claim C.3. Pred_id 5 explicitly states the claim uses ≥ but the proof establishes ≤, and notes the inconsistency in how it's applied in Theorem 3.1's proof.

The ground truth concerns overstating generality by claiming results work for arbitrary convex sets when central symmetry is required. Pred_id 12 discusses range vs. Bregman-rate conflation but not the central symmetry requirement issue.

The ground truth concerns missing computational complexity analysis for maintaining distributions over continuous P. None of the findings address computational cost or efficiency claims in this specific way.

Both identify the incorrect 1/T normalization in the calibration error definition. Pred_id 8 explicitly states Section 2.1 includes 1/T in the definition while the rest of the paper uses the unnormalized convention, creating a factor-of-T inconsistency.

Both identify the incorrect exponent in Theorem 4.3. Pred_id 4 explicitly states the theorem uses d^{1/7} but the proof and Theorem 4.1 give d^{1/14}, matching the ground truth's fabrication of the exponent.
